{"id": "aeca6643-a0a8-41bb-b51d-766e70df00b3", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Based on current EKS documentation:

- **Check series/category:** These are all reported under the **`UPGRADE_READINESS`** insight category — officially called "upgrade insights." This includes kube-proxy version skew, kubelet version skew, and add-on (EKS add-on) compatibility checks. (EKS's other category, `MISCONFIGURATION`, covers Hybrid Nodes setup issues — "configuration insights" — which is a distinct series, not the one these skew/compatibility checks fall into.)

- **"CP checks" label:** No — AWS's own terminology for this category is **`UPGRADE_READINESS`** / "upgrade insights," not "CP checks." There's no AWS documentation calling these "CP checks," so that label wouldn't be accurate for a grading rubric. If your dashboard is using "CP" as shorthand for "Control Plane," that's not how EKS categorizes these insights — kube-proxy/kubelet skew and add-on compatibility are component/version-compatibility checks within `UPGRADE_READINESS`, not a distinct "control plane" series.

One nuance worth flagging for grading: AWS expanded this catalog in Dec 2024 specifically to add kubelet/kube-proxy/add-on compatibility checks into `UPGRADE_READINESS`, and more recently (2026) introduced version rollback, which also evaluates readiness insights (API compatibility, version skew, add-on compatibility, cluster health) before a rollback — all still under the same upgrade-insights umbrella, not a separate "CP" series.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
